positives: If this company sold everything it owns and paid off everything it owes, there would be real money left over. It owns more than it owes.
It hasn't borrowed too much money - what it owes is less than what the business itself is worth.
It has plenty of cash and other easy-to-sell things on hand - more than twice enough to cover the bills it owes over the next year.
worries: Counting all the money it uses to run the business, it isn't making any profit right now.
After paying for everything it needs to run and grow the business, it's actually spending more cash than it's bringing in.
The share of each sale it gets to keep as profit has been getting worse over the last few years.

This business makes less profit on the money it uses than that money actually costs to raise. That usually means competitors aren't held back from doing the same thing it does - no real moat protecting it.

The 10-Q XBRL data references both a '2024 Restructuring Plan' and a '2025 Restructuring Plan,' suggesting the company has undertaken multiple rounds of restructuring.
The 10-Q data indicates a disposal/sale of the Altera business (equity method investee), reflecting a divestiture of a prior business unit.

The 10-Q references large government-related arrangements (Department of Commerce, Ireland SCIP, Arizona SCIP variable interest entities), indicating reliance on government funding or support structures tied to manufacturing facilities.
